back: Adds two bits: sum S = A XOR B, carry C = A AND B. It has no carry in.
Adds two bits and a carry in, giving a sum and a carry out. Built from two half adders and an OR gate.
Half adder 1 adds A and B. Half adder 2 adds its sum to Cin to give S. An OR gate combines the two carries to give Cout.
A chain of full adders where the carry out of each stage is the carry in of the next; slow for many bits because carries ripple through.
A circuit with two stable states that stores one bit.
S = 1: set (Q = 1). R = 1: reset (Q = 0). S = R = 0: hold. S = R = 1: invalid.
J = K = 0: hold. J = 1, K = 0: set. J = 0, K = 1: reset. J = K = 1: toggle.

front: How does a NOR SR flip-flop hold a bit?
back: The output of each NOR gate feeds back into the other, so with S = R = 0 the outputs keep their last state.
Registers and static memory (SRAM): each flip-flop stores one bit.
